title: Fine-grained descending control of steering in walking Drosophila.
source_locator: Results, 'Different descending neurons drive distinctive leg gestures'; Fig. 4A-C; Fig. S6G left
quote: a pulse of light triggered an ipsilateral turn, with no change in forward velocity as compared with controls (Figure 4A).
mapping_basis: Paper uses the Namiki type name DNa02, which is a MANC type name; hemidrivers R75C10AD/R87D07DBD = SS00730, listed as DNa02 in driver_lines.csv.
stimulation: 620/60 nm light, 0.09 mW/mm2, 200 ms pulses (randomly interleaved with 2 s pulses, which had similar transient effects)
type_coverage: one of the two DNa02 cells (unilateral, SPARC genetic mosaic)
sensory_condition: norpA[P24] (blind) flies walking on an air-supported ball; head capsule closed
other_cell_types: lobula visual neurons (one type, ~2 cells per hemisphere)
a few abdominal ganglion cells in a subset of flies
coordination_notes: Shortened stride length (mainly the return stroke) of all three ipsilateral legs; less consistent contralateral effects; step direction of front and middle legs shifted to pull the body into the turn.
notes: Trials were included only if the fly was walking (mean forward velocity >= 1 mm/s around the stimulus), so this is a turn in a fly that was already walking; the leg-rhythm fields are not_assessed (PROTOCOL section 3). Controls were genetically identical flies with no CsChrimson in either DNa02.

title: Fine-grained descending control of steering in walking Drosophila.
source_locator: Results, 'Different descending neurons drive distinctive leg gestures'; Fig. S6A-C
quote: Bilateral activation of DNa02 instead triggered a decrease in forward velocity without a change in the heading direction (Figure S6A).
mapping_basis: Paper uses the Namiki type name DNa02, which is a MANC type name; hemidrivers R75C10AD/R87D07DBD = SS00730, listed as DNa02 in driver_lines.csv.
type_coverage: both DNa02 cells (bilateral expression in the SPARC mosaic)
sensory_condition: norpA[P24] (blind) flies walking on an air-supported ball; head capsule closed
other_cell_types: lobula visual neurons (one type, ~2 cells per hemisphere)
a few abdominal ganglion cells in a subset of flies
coordination_notes: Stride length shortened bilaterally, mainly through a shorter return stroke; power stroke little affected (Fig. S6B-C).
notes: Kept separate from record 0001 because the outcome differs (slowing rather than turning). Trials were included only if the fly was already walking, so the leg-rhythm fields are not_assessed. behaviour_category 'other' = slowing of forward walking.

title: Fine-grained descending control of steering in walking Drosophila.
quote: In flies where this ascending neuron expressed CsChrimson, regardless of whether DNg13 expressed CsChrimson, light stopped locomotion.
mapping_basis: Paper uses the Namiki type name DNg13, which is a MANC type name; hemidrivers VT027166AD/VT009857DBD = SS02259, listed as DNg13 in driver_lines.csv.
stimulation: not stated separately; the same optogenetic rig as the DNa02 experiments (620/60 nm)
other_cell_types: an ascending neuron labelled by the same line (unnamed)
penetrance: stopping occurred in every fly with CsChrimson in the ascending neuron, regardless of DNg13 expression
notes: The authors attribute the stopping to the off-target ascending neuron, not to DNg13: flies stopped regardless of whether DNg13 expressed CsChrimson. Too few flies had DNg13-only expression, so no DNg13-specific optogenetic result is reported. The paper's other DNg13 perturbation, current injection by whole-cell patch clamp (Fig. 4G-I: ipsiversive turning, longer contralateral strides), is neither optogenetic nor thermogenetic activation, so it is not recorded. Treat this record as an off-target-confounded observation.

title: A neural circuit for context-dependent multimodal signaling in Drosophila.
source_locator: Results, 'Stationarity is necessary and sufficient to drive vibrations in males'; Fig. 3C-D; Table 1; Methods, Optogenetics
quote: inducing female walking by optogenetically activating the DNp28 neurons55,56 nearly abolished vibrations (Fig. 3C, D).
mapping_basis: The paper names the cells DNp28 but gives the line as SS01587 (R11H10-p65.AD; VT033947-GAL4.DBD), which driver_lines.csv maps to DNp29 (Namiki 2018 and the eLife 107450 table); the DNp28 lines in the kit are other lines (SS01056, SS01589, SS01590). The explicit genotype was preferred over the label, which may be a typo; the paper gives no anatomy to decide.
stimulation: 625 nm red LED, 89 mW/cm2, 5 s pulses every 30 s, 30 trials
sensory_condition: freely walking female courted by a wild-type male in a 44 mm chamber; room light off
n_flies_note: DNp28-Chrimson+ (retinal-fed) N = 9 pairs; controls: DNp28-Gal4+ N = 4, UAS-Chrimson+ N = 5, DNp28-Chrimson- N = 7
notes: Locomotion was scored only from body velocity (no leg tracking), so the legs are coded yes with medium confidence (PROTOCOL section 3). Fig. 3C shows female velocity rising from about 1 mm/s to about 12 mm/s during the light (the male follows). The mapping conflict between the DNp28 label and the SS01587 genotype (DNp29 in the kit) is noted in notes.md; if adjudicators trust the label, manc_type would be DNp28.
